unit.name: From long recordings to windowed labels
unit.description: The instructor shows how to transform a small number of long annotated clips into many binary training examples and uses the resulting failure mode to teach class imbalance in event detection.
unit.summary: The proposed labeling scheme turns each long recording into multiple short windows and marks a window positive only when it ends right after the speaker finishes "Robert, turn on" [ts=1661s] [ts=1776s]. This turns roughly 100 long clips into around 3,000 binary examples, which is operationally convenient for training a classifier [ts=1775s] [ts=1798s]. The first model then reports 97% accuracy while producing zero detections, revealing that the dataset is so skewed that always predicting the negative class looks strong under the naive metric [ts=1813s] [ts=1860s]. The segment uses this to motivate rebalancing strategies rather than trusting headline accuracy alone [ts=1914s] [ts=1978s].

key_points.text: Use sliding windows over longer audio clips and label a window positive when the trigger phrase has just finished.
Windowing can expand about 100 long clips into about 3,000 binary examples.
A 97% accurate classifier can still be useless if it always predicts the majority class.
Severe class imbalance is a common source of misleading metrics in trigger detection.

kp_catalog.name: Sliding-window supervision for event detection
kp_catalog.description: A labeling scheme that converts long sequences into many local binary examples aligned to when an event has just occurred.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lecture gives a concrete transformation from long audio recordings to short labeled windows and uses it as the backbone of training data construction [ts=1661s] [ts=1776s].

kp_catalog.name: Class imbalance can invalidate naive accuracy
kp_catalog.description: The principle that highly skewed labels can make aggregate accuracy misleading and require reweighting, duplication, or relabeling fixes.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Class imbalance is a core diagnostic failure mode that can invalidate naive metrics.
